title: Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint remanded to lower court for new hearing; Commission unable to adjudicate because BCO 43-5 record not complied with and minutes inadequate. Assembly approved and accepted that judgment. Assembly separately adopted 238–131 a recommendation that the BCO does not envisage ordination of a candidate expressly to pastoral services in a church of another denomination. Requested annulment and ordination order not granted; merits not reached.
first_summary: Trinity Church complained that Grace Presbytery's substitute motion improperly delayed Adrian Pater's ordination until he was called to PCA work. The Judicial Commission could not adjudicate and returned the matter to the lower court for a new hearing. The General Assembly adopted the report.
summary: Trinity Church complained that Grace Presbytery's July 9, 1976 substitute motion, delaying Adrian Pater's ordination until he was called to PCA work, was an out-of-order reconsideration. The Judicial Commission did not reach the merits: because the BCO 43-5 record was not complied with and minutes were inadequate, it returned the whole matter to the lower court for a new hearing. The Assembly accepted that judgment and separately adopted, 238–131, a recommendation that the BCO does not envisage ordination expressly for pastoral service in another denomination.
